Trapping the Center: A Journey into Geometric Probability

math
probability
geometry
What is the probability that n random points on a circle contain the center?
Author

Alex Shao

Published

December 18, 2025

Imagine you have a circular piece of plywood. You randomly hammer 6 nails into the very edge of the circle. If you wrap a rubber band around those nails, what are the odds that the center of the wood is trapped inside that rubber band?

This is a pretty classic problem in the field of geometric probability. The idea was inspired by a video I saw online, but a detailed write-up can also be found at Brainstellar (along with some other really interesting puzzles!)

Interactive Simulation

Code 
import { createInteractiveCircle } from "./visualization.js"

app = {
  // 1. Setup Layout
  const container = html`<div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center;">
    <div class="controls-container">
       <div id="slider-container"></div>
       <button class="randomize-btn">Randomize Positions</button>
    </div>
    <div id="canvas-container"></div>
  </div>`;

  const sliderContainer = container.querySelector("#slider-container");
  const canvasContainer = container.querySelector("#canvas-container");
  const randBtn = container.querySelector("button");

  // 2. State Variables
  let currentLogic = null; 
  let currentN = 6; // Keep track of the last valid N
  
  // 3. Helper to Create/Reset Canvas
  function updateCanvas(n, mode) {
    // IMPORTANT: Dispose of old logic to remove event listeners
    if (currentLogic) currentLogic.dispose();
    
    canvasContainer.innerHTML = "";
    const c = DOM.canvas(400, 400);
    canvasContainer.appendChild(c);
    
    currentLogic = createInteractiveCircle(c, n, mode);
    currentN = n;
  }

  // 4. Initialize Controls
  const sliderWrapper = Inputs.range([3, 12], {value: 6, step: 1, label: "Points (n)"});
  sliderContainer.appendChild(sliderWrapper);

  const rangeInput = sliderWrapper.querySelector("input[type='range']");
  const numberInput = sliderWrapper.querySelector("input[type='number']");

  // 5. Validation Function
  // Returns valid integer or null if invalid
  function parseAndValidate(value) {
    const num = Number(value);
    
    // Check 1: Must be a number and an integer (no decimals like 3.4)
    if (isNaN(num) || !Number.isInteger(num)) return null;
    
    // Check 2: Range [3, 12]
    if (num < 3 || num > 12) return null;
    
    return num;
  }

  // 6. Handle Number Input Changes
  numberInput.addEventListener("input", () => {
    const val = parseAndValidate(numberInput.value);
    
    if (val !== null) {
      // Valid Input: Sync slider, clear error, update canvas
      numberInput.style.border = "";
      numberInput.style.outline = "";
      rangeInput.value = val;
      updateCanvas(val, "even");
    } else {
      // Invalid Input: Red border, DO NOT update canvas
      numberInput.style.border = "2px solid red";
      numberInput.style.outline = "none";
    }
  });

  // 7. Handle Slider Changes
  // Slider is naturally constrained, so we trust it updates the number input
  rangeInput.addEventListener("input", () => {
    const val = rangeInput.valueAsNumber;
    numberInput.value = val;
    
    // Clear any previous error states from manual typing
    numberInput.style.border = "";
    numberInput.style.outline = "";
    
    updateCanvas(val, "even");
  });
  
  // 8. Handle Blur (Reset if invalid)
  numberInput.addEventListener("blur", () => {
    const val = parseAndValidate(numberInput.value);
    if (val === null) {
      // Revert to last known valid state
      numberInput.value = currentN;
      numberInput.style.border = "";
      numberInput.style.outline = "";
    }
  });

  // 9. Randomize Button
  randBtn.onclick = () => {
    if (currentLogic) currentLogic.randomize();
  };

  // 10. Initial Render
  updateCanvas(6, "even");

  return container;
}

The Mathematical Derivation

Instead of calculating the probability of the center being inside, we calculate the probability of the complement: the center being outside.

1. The Semicircle Condition

The center of the circle lies outside the polygon if and only if all points lie within the same arc (a semicircle).
